newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer settles U.S. dispute with Barr. [CORRECTED 10:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bayer settles U.S. dispute with Barr. [CORRECTED 10:42 GMT]

text.p: German chemicals group Bayer AG said on Friday it and its U.S. subsidiary Bayer Corporation had reached an agreement with Barr Laboratories Inc to end litigation over the U.S. patent on Ciprofloxacin.

Under the agreement, Barr, a U.S. maker of generic drugs, acknowledges the validity of Bayer's worldwide patents on Ciprofloxacin, an ingredient that fights infections, Bayer said in a statement. Bayer will pay $24.5 million in 1997 each to Barr and Rugby Laboratories Inc, which has supported Barr during the dispute.
Ciprofloxacin is used to treat lower respiratory, skin, bone and joint, and urinary tract infections.
Barr had challenged the validity of certain patents held by Bayer for the tablet version of Ciprofloxacin. There is also an intravenous version.
Bayer generates annual sales of $1.3 billion (corrects denomination from marks) worldwide from Ciprofloxacin in tablet and intravenous form, a Bayer spokesman said.

"This settlement shows that we didn't want a long court case, you never know how long they will take," Bayer spokesman Thomas Reinert said in response to a Reuter enquiry. "The product is important to us."

Under the deal, Bayer has the choice of either making annual payments to Barr and Rugby totalling $49 million in the years 1998 through to 2003, when Bayer's patent expires. Alternatively, it can supply the firms with the drug which they can then market, provided that they acknowledge Bayer's patent, Reinert said.
Ciprofloxacin is the world's leading broad band antibiotic, Reinert said.
